title: POC runbook: customer workshop + on‑prem requirements
summary: Working runbook and notes for a customer POC workshop where we evaluate an on-prem deployment (air-gapped or limited egress). Focus: capture infra/security constraints, acceptance criteria, and a lightweight test plan that solutions engineering can run with site ops.
objective: Run a 2-day onsite/remote hybrid workshop that collects enough operational detail to scope a validated on-prem POC and produce: 1) install/run checklist, 2) minimal performance baseline, 3) security and upgrade constraints, and 4) a signed-off acceptance criteria doc.
audience: Customer platform ops, solutions engineering SE, customer security/compliance, Redwood deployment engineer
workshop_agenda: Day 0 (pre-work): share questionnaire + quick inventory (OS, hypervisor/K8s, number of GPUs, storage)
Day 1 morning: introductions, high-level architecture review, constraint mapping (network, 3rd-party access, certs)
Day 1 afternoon: hands-on infra discovery - run inventory scripts, verify driver/firmware versions, check available ports and NAT settings
Day 2 morning: security deep dive (KMS/HSM, signing, airgap update expectations)
Day 2 afternoon: operational run-through: deployment steps, metrics, rollback, demo smoke tests, schedule follow-ups
infrastructure_requirements: Compute: at least 1 node with 4xA100-40GB or 2xA40 (or equivalent) for the initial perf baseline; note: support for heterogeneous pools required
OS: RHEL 8.8 or Ubuntu 22.04 LTS preferred; minimum kernel 5.15 for NVIDIA driver compatibility
Container runtime: Docker 24.x or containerd; if air-gapped, confirm signed container images and local registry procedure
Drivers: NVIDIA driver 535+ and CUDA 12.x for optimized kernels; confirm admin permission to install drivers or that drivers are preinstalled
Storage: fast NVMe for model weights and KV cache; fallback NFS or SAN is acceptable but we must capture throughput numbers (IOPS, latency)
Networking: allowed egress to specific Redwood endpoints if not fully air-gapped; if strict airgap, plan for registry mirroring and package transfer process
Load balancing: ingress LB or bastion for admin access, DNS entries (can be hosts file for POC), cert management policy
security_requirements: KMS integration: customer-managed KMS required for Private mode; document API/protocol and offline key import steps
HSM: if HSM is used, capture vendor, SDK, and access policy; note that HSM may block automated key rotation during POC
Certificate strategy: support for customer CA-signed certs; bring steps to install certs into JVM/OS trust stores
Signed artifacts: customer must accept signed RPMs/containers or allow us to provide signed tarballs for manual install
Least privilege: deployment should run under a non-root service account where possible; document sudo needs
Telemetry: by default we push anonymized metrics; for air-gapped POCs, we replace with a Prometheus pushgateway or local Prometheus pull. Explicit opt-in required for any outbound telemetry.
operational_requirements: Service user accounts for deployment engineer and SE with sudo/assumed-permissions during install window
Maintenance window: schedule 2-hour block for initial install and separate 1-hour block for driver/kernel upgrades
Backup: plan for model weight backup location (on-prem S3 or object store) and snapshot cadence
Monitoring: Prometheus + node exporters + a lightweight shipper (fluentbit) to a local aggregator; if remote Redwood Console is not allowed, provide offline logs bundle instructions
Upgrade plan: offline patch path using signed bundles and verification checksums; customer to confirm approval gate for each minor version
Runbooks: step-by-step restart and rollback steps with exact commands and timeout thresholds
runbook_outline: Pre-checks: validate kernel, driver, container runtime, storage mount points
Mirror registry (air-gapped): steps to pull, sign, and mirror containers to local registry with example commands
Install sequence: install drivers -> install runtime -> deploy redis/cache -> deploy model service -> run smoke test
Smoke tests: health endpoints, sample inference with seeded prompt, KV cache warmup for 10k tokens
Perf test: run curated workload that iterates token lengths 32/128/512 and capture p50/p95/p99 latencies and tokens/sec
Metrics collection: configure Prometheus scrape, verify retention, export bundle
Rollback: stop service, restore previous container tag, restore weights if needed, clear caches
acceptance_criteria: Functional: service returns expected structured output for 10 seed prompts (golden set) without errors
Performance: p95 latency under 600ms for 1 concurrent request baseline (adjust per customer scale) and sustained throughput within 20% of hosted profile
Reliability: 1 hour continuous run without crashes and no unhandled OOMs; memory/KV cache within documented bounds
Security: KMS integration verified (key fetch and encryption flows), signed artifacts validated, no outbound telemetry without explicit opt-in
Operational: deployment and rollback executed end-to-end by site ops following the runbook within target windows
open_questions: Does the customer allow periodic outbound connections to 'updates.redwood.ai' for security patches, or is a manual patch process required?
Is there an existing private container registry we must mirror to, or do we set up a temporary local registry?
Can infrastructure team perform an ephemeral driver/kernel upgrade during the POC window if needed?
Are there encryption-at-rest requirements for model artifacts beyond the default object-store encryption?
Which monitoring system is canonical (Prometheus push vs. pull) and what retention do they maintain for test artifacts?
action_items: SEs: send pre-work questionnaire to customer 5 days before workshop (inventory + admin contacts)
Infra: confirm GPU and driver inventory, and reserve maintenance window for potential kernel upgrade
Security: collate KMS/HSM contact + policy and test key material transfer method
Engineering: prepare signed offline bundle (containers + RPMs) and checksum file, store on encrypted USB as fallback
Ops: prepare Prometheus/Fluentbit local stacks and example config templates to drop into customer's environment
notes: Notes-to-self: bring a short demo that runs without external egress in <30m. Pack USB with signed bundles and an on-call list. Expect customers to ask about model refresh cadence and cost math — have a one-pager ready. After workshop, capture exact firewall ports and NAT rules and convert to a minimal acceptance checklist for SOC review. Follow up items -> create JIRA epic and link back.
